label: 1-2 steps after an early original-phase t
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase on the one or two steps right after the letter t is input, and only when t was early in the sequence (fires at steps 1-5, essentially never at step 6 or later). It is strongest on the step right after t: prev_tok==t alone covers 98% of the top activation quartile and 71% of activation mass. It is weaker two steps after, and only faint traces remain three steps after. The top activations come from repeated t (t t x), which stacks the response. Activation does not depend on which token is currently input. Never fires in the copy phase; fires weakly at the delimiter (1.5% of mass). Does not fire for a t that appears late (step 5 or later) in long sequences, which is where most of the remaining false positives come from. The missed activations are low-magnitude (3% of mass).

issues: Minor wording: the very highest activations come from the step two after the first t in a 't t x' run (prev_tok==t and prev2_tok==t, e.g. 'q t t [j:0.99]'). The second t itself reaches only about 0.56. 'Repeated t' is still accurate.

Missed activations hold 5.3% of activation mass on test, not the ~3% claimed. They are mostly tiny background activations (about 0.01-0.07) at steps 3-5 where no t has appeared. That class has rate 2.7% and fires mostly in the bottom quartile, so it is scattered noise. Lowest-quartile coverage is only 15%.

False positives are spread across positions rather than forming a class. Predicting t+2 when the token at step 0 is t (step 2) has precision 0.89, and steps 3, 4 and 5 have 0.90 and 0.84. Dropping the t+2 term at step 2 lowers test F1 to 0.759.

All other claims check out on dev: no copy-phase activations (0 of 2.73M steps), delimiter 1.5% of mass, prev_tok==t with t<=5 gives 70% of mass and 98% of the top quartile, a late t (t>=6) has precision 0.10 and 0.4% of mass, and three steps after t gives 1.4% of mass (faint).
